newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to let South Africa into Lome Convention.
newsitem.headline: EU to let South Africa into Lome Convention.

text.p: Spain said on Monday it would lift its veto on South Africa joining the Lome Convention, opening Pretoria's way into the European Union's main trade arrangement with the developing world next month.
Diplomats said the move came after EU ministers received a letter from Pretoria pledging to continue negotiations on a broader trade package.

Negotiations on the trade element of the package -- designed to give South Africa preferential treatment in its commercial dealings with the EU -- have bogged down, mainly over agricultural and wine exports.
Most EU countries viewed the Lome move as a way of encouraging the talks with Pretoria.
But Madrid blocked the idea of putting South Africa on a fast track to join the Convention because of concerns that it would slow a deal on fisheries.
A Spanish diplomat said, however, that his country was now lifting its block because of the commitment from South Africa.
The ministers were to release a statement later outlining their view that the Lome decision had been taken as part of a broader move to reach a deal with Pretoria.
Membership of Lome -- expected now to come at a meeting on April 24 -- will give South Africa access to preferential trade treatment and aid.
